{"id": "e863dc85-458e-447a-866a-e995b2303540", "role": "assistant", "content": [{"text": "Yes, provisioned concurrency is the right fix for this pattern. A few checks first.

**Why it fits**
- Your numbers point to cold starts. `ModelSetupTime` only emits datapoints when a request has to start a new container. You see none in busy hours and a p99 of about 9s on the first request after 15 minutes idle. That means warm capacity absorbs traffic when it's busy, and only the idle-to-active transition is slow.
- Provisioned concurrency keeps a set number of instances warm, so those first requests skip the cold start.

**How to configure it**
- Set `ProvisionedConcurrency` in the variant's `ServerlessConfig`. Per the API reference it must be 1 or more and no more than `MaxConcurrency`. Your `MaxConcurrency` is 5, so you can set it to anything from 1 to 5.
- Start small, at 1 or 2, since your problem is the first request after idle and not high concurrency. Requests above the provisioned amount still use on-demand capacity and can still cold start, up to `MaxConcurrency`.
- You'll need a new endpoint config and an `UpdateEndpoint` call to roll it out. You can also use `UpdateEndpointWeightsAndCapacities` to change the value on a live endpoint, but check the docs for your setup.

**Trade-offs**
- **Cost:** provisioned capacity is billed for the time it's provisioned, whether or not requests arrive. This changes the "pay only when invoked" model of serverless. I didn't pull current pricing, so check the SageMaker pricing page before you commit.
- **Idle periods:** if the endpoint really is idle overnight or on weekends, you can use Application Auto Scaling to scale provisioned concurrency up and down on a schedule or by utilization. This keeps the cost lower.
- **Memory size:** 4096 MB is fine. Larger memory also gives more vCPU, which can shorten model load, but it won't remove a 9s cold start.

**Alternatives if cost matters more than latency**
- **Keep-warm pings:** send a synthetic invocation more often than every 15 minutes, for example from EventBridge on a schedule. It's cheap, but it's a workaround. It only keeps about one container warm, and it adds noise to your metrics.
- **Shrink the cold start:** reduce model artifact size, trim container startup work, and lazy-load only what you need. This helps either way.
- **Real-time endpoint:** if you need consistently low latency around the clock, a small always-on real-time instance may cost about the same as provisioned concurrency and is more predictable.

**How to verify**
After the change, watch `ModelSetupTime` and `OverheadLatency`. For the first request after idle you should see `ModelSetupTime` datapoints largely disappear, or drop sharply. You can also compare p99 `ModelLatency` and end-to-end latency across the same idle windows.

I can't see the account, so this relies on the config and metrics you described. If you want me to dig into the endpoint or its traffic pattern, the account would need to be connected to this agent space.", "type": "text"}], "created_at": null}
